alex: quick heads-up — ran a profiling sweep against canary yesterday and p50 for short requests jumped ~18ms for the small-batch path.
jia: yikes. same kernel selector config as before?
alex: yes, we changed heuristic last week to prefer conv-optim kernel when batch_size >= 4, sequence <= 48. suspect selector picks conv-optim more often now and it hurts small-batch latency.
sam: can you paste the query you used to find the regression?
alex: sure — prometheus query: `histogram_quantile(0.5, sum(rate(kernel_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, kernel, route))`
alex: and a quick log snippet from the profiling run:```
[2026-03-10T03:12:11Z] route=/chat/stream kernel=conv-optim batch=2 seq=32 p50=42.3ms
[2026-03-10T03:12:11Z] route=/chat/stream kernel=matmul-vec batch=2 seq=32 p50=24.1ms
```
jia: that looks consistent with kernel mismatch. conv-optim is great at throughput but has higher tail for tiny batches.
lisa: did we account for KV cache hit distribution in the trace? small sequences that hit cache will be more sensitive.
alex: KV hit rates were ~72% for that workload. I pulled a flame graph — more overhead in kernel dispatch and memcpy with conv-optim for these shapes.
devon: maybe the selector needs a micro-shape table: prefer matmul-vec for batch <=2 and seq <=64 even if conv-optim has better bench numbers for larger batches.
sam: agree. we should also sanity-check billing alignment: per-token accounting assumes kernel latency map => cost. If kernel choice flips, per-token unit cost numbers drift.
lisa: I flagged a dashboard inconsistency earlier — per-route unit cost in /ops/costs spike but aggregate billing didn't change. looks like we double-counted prefix tokens when we switched sampling.
alex: link to dashboard: https://redwood.internal/d/rt-perf/per-unit-latency?orgId=1&var-route=chat/stream
jia: propose quick experiment: revert heuristic on canary for 1 hour, compare p50/p95, and validate cost-per-token delta.
devon: +1. I'll open a short-lived feature flag: `selector.strict_small_batch_v1=false` and roll to 10% first.
deploy-bot: deploy started by devon: rollout to canary (10%) — id: deploy-4389
sam: while it's rolling, let's add a metric to capture kernel selection distribution per-route: `count_over_time(kernel_selected{route=~".*chat.*"}[5m])` and wire it to the perf channel.
lisa: and add kv_miss_weighted_latency: `sum(rate(kv_miss_latency_sum[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_miss_count[5m]))` so we can attribute overhead to cache misses.
jia: action items: 1) devon: flag + rollback plan — 10% canary 2) alex: collect kernel distribution and KV hit slices for last 48h 3) sam: validate cost-per-token alignment after revert 4) lisa: create dashboard panel with kernel distribution and kv_miss_weighted_latency
alex: noted. I'll upload the profiling flamegraphs to the perf docs and paste link in the ticket.
devon: deploy done to 10% canary, monitoring p50 now.
deploy-bot: deploy successful to canary (10%) — id: deploy-4389
alex: early signals: p50 dropped back ~15ms for canary requests routed to matmul-vec path. can confirm kernel selector change is causal.
sam: great. please keep the canary running for 2 hours and then either roll forward or revert based on cost alignment.
lisa: opened dashboard PR: https://git.internal/redwood/dashboards/pull/214 — adds kernel-selection heatmap and per-route cost breakdown.
jia: thanks all. keeping this thread pinned until we have final rollout decision. :thumbsup:
